text:
alex: heads-up — long-run job on prod-bench is showing steady memory growth (~2.7GB -> 4.2GB over 36h) even with stable QPS. suspect KV cache fragmentation + reuse hole patterns when contexts exceed ~120k tokens. attaching profile summary below.

priya: ouch. do we have flame graphs or heap histograms?

alex: pasted the top lines from heap-profile:
```
Total KV cache allocations: 1.8M objects
Unique block sizes: [512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192] (heavy at 2048 and 4096)
Free list buckets with >1M entries: 2048(4), 4096(6)
Fragmentation estimate: ~18% (unusable gaps due to alignment/slot mismatch)
Hot paths: put_kv(), evict_l2(), reuse_probe()
```

jamal: interesting — lots of churn at 2k/4k. that smells like our mini-chunk allocator refusing to coalesce because of sticky LRU pointers. are long contexts creating many short-lived KV entries that later outlive others?

alex: yes. sequence-level tests show many small suffix KV writes interleaved with very large ones. allocator picks 2048 for most of them but gaps left between larger 8k blocks. over time you get many tiny holes that never get reused.

wei: can you repro locally with the replay harness? I can run a targeted debug build with extra freelist logging.

alex: repro script attached to the thread (run_replay --long-context --seed=42). yields the growth in ~3h on my dev box.

priya: quick thought: do we have per-bucket age segregation? if we promote older entries to a different bucket we could reduce interleaving. or use epochal reuse: allocate per-epoch arenas and reclaim whole arenas once the epoch advances for long-lived contexts.

jamal: epochal arenas could be low-cost to free but might increase peak memory since we don't reclaim within epoch. tradeoff depends on epoch length. for rolling workloads maybe 30s epoch is fine.

wei: alternatively, change block-size quantization: round allocations to a smaller set (powers-of-two) so fewer distinct sizes => easier coalescing. we'd need to measure external fragmentation vs internal waste.

alex: I tried a prototype that forces quantize -> {512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192} (down from a wide distribution) and it reduced fragmentation estimate to ~7% in the replay harness and eliminated growth. downside: increased internal waste on many 1.2k allocations.

priya: what's the perf/latency impact? any allocation hotpath regressions?

alex: noop for steady-state p50/p95. allocation path slightly faster due to simpler bucket lookup. needs more load testing.

jamal: what about background compaction? run incremental compaction when free-bucket entropy crosses threshold. compact only low-activity slabs to avoid throughput impact.

wei: compactor needs to be careful with locking. we can snapshot a free list and migrate live entries in small batches. add a tunable: compaction_batch_ms and max_cpu_pct.

priya: propose we run three experiments: (A) quantized allocator prototype on staging for 24h, (B) epochal arena with 30s/120s settings, (C) background incremental compactor with conservative defaults. each should include heap profiles + perf counters (evictions/sec, reuse-hit-rate, avg-alloc-latency).

alex: agreed. I'll push A as a canary today (branch: kv-quantize-canary). cc @ci-bot to run the canary pipeline.

ci-bot: triggered pipeline kv-quantize-canary (staging) — build queued. :gear:

jamal: I'll start wiring the compactor proto into a feature branch (kv-incremental-compactor). will include lock-free handoff where possible.

wei: I'll reproduce the long-run replay with the quantize build and collect baseline + change. need logs: export KV_FREELIST_DUMP=1 and KV_COMPACT_DEBUG=1.

priya: also add a simple metric: kv.fragmentation_gap_bytes and kv.fragmentation_pct so we can alert if it drifts.

alex: adding alerts + dashboard panel. if canary looks good we'll rollout to a small subset of prod nodes tomorrow.

wei: one more note — paging behavior: when fragmentation increases we observed more page-fault churn on nodes with NUMA. compaction reduced remote pages. include numa-aware placement in the follow-up.

jamal: good call. I'll add a NUMA-aware hint to the compactor design doc.

alex: thanks team — action items captured: alex -> canary push + dashboard, wei -> replay + logs, jamal -> compactor proto, priya -> experiment matrix + alert thresholds. we'll sync in tomorrow stand if needed. :thumbsup:
